For me, this season is having better writing that the second one. The dialogs and situations feel more "natural, raw and aggressive". Hughie was a let down for me, it wasn't until episode 03 that I regain some respect for him. His change of attitude felt so weird. Also, what happened to Maeve? She is barely on screen. But as always, the series is still amazing to me, every moment brings me a laugh or a nervous feeling. So many plot twists have occurred on episode 03 that my brain could blow away (lol).

I am very happy that MM has more focus this season. Laz Alonso is so likeable and I am excited to see more of story. Starlight is one of my favorite characters and she continues to be this season. I feel bad for her. As the spy of the group. she has spent the entirety of the show under so much pressure and I don't think she can take it anymore. Hughie and Starlight are one of the few couples on television that I actually like honestly. They are adorable together. Erin Moriarty is a great actress, I feel like she doesn't get enough credit. I love Kimiko but I hope that she gets more of a substantial storyline. Her personal story feels similar to last season's. Frenchie is great and I hope his storyline is done well this season.  I watched Grace Randolph's review (which confirmed why I hate her, btw) and she said his storyline is about abuse, I assume from his father and given what we have seen I don't know how to take that. She says it was done poorly but other reviewers have said Frenchie, MM, and Kimiko have some of the most touching moments of the season. I don't believe that the writers of the show would handle an issue that they didn't understand. I still don't understand his motivation for fighting the supes though. Everyone else has a specific, personal reason but he just got dragged into it. I mean, they should be hated for obvious reasons but it's strange there isn't a more personal story there. I liked seeing Grace's backstory, but after MM called her out for what the CIA has done I'll admit I care less about her. She's done plenty of terrible things and doesn't have a right to judge Butcher and other characters. I was excited to see Jensen Ackles, but Soldier Boy did not impress me in the flashbacks. He just felt like a caricature. I hope that it improves in later episodes. The writers overall feel like they are doing a much better job than last season and everything feels meticulously put together.

Some contact yes, and one of their founders and his original recruits did have close ties to the KGB, but the myth that they were a "puppet" or "satellite" was the US's primary justification for any sort of brutal overt or covert action anywhere in the world to overthrow 'the Reds' – and the CIA-trained-and-backed Contras were especially fucking monstrous. This season was underwhelming. I know everyone loved every little thing in each episode and felt that it kept getting better with each episode. That's your prerogative. I thought it was underwhelming from the start, yet by the end, the beginning (first two episodes or so) seemed way better; the finale was the worst episode. It pretty much undermined the entire season, resetting everything back to the beginning, back to the status quo, and that left a sour taste on every episode prior. I get that Homelander IS the show alongside Butcher, but the dancing around and jumping through hoops that the writers are doing to extend and prolong the inevitable defeat of Homelander is getting tiring. It makes everything else (which already wasn't that captivating) seem more pointless. Nothing feels different; it's all the same behind the illusion of the presentations. Now, while a sense of underwhelmingness was present from the start, I liked the addition of leveling the playing field, the build-up to introducing Soldier Boy, including the character himself, and, of course, Butcher and Homelander/the acting performances by Karl Urban and Antony Starr. Yeah, there were the similarity undertones with what he did to Hughie, the karma that went along with it, not to mention the social commentary. I still didn't care, let alone care about his redemption. Maeve was irrelevant for most of the season. The Deep and his scenes are entertaining, but a meal for the runtime of each episode. Frenchie's plotline with Little Nina was underdeveloped and only there as a means for The Boys to be able to go to Russia. The thing with M.M. and Soldier Boy, especially its conclusion that amounted to M.M. bringing the heat with his words (but was goofy instead), was underwhelming and felt there for social commentary purposes, and it didn't seem developed enough. This season was only serviceable, but the show is practically a guilty pleasure at this point. Everyone else will continue treating it as the best thing in existence, while I'll continue to bring that up and feel the opposite. I don't have high hopes for the fourth season, and I didn't for this season. But I'll still watch it. I'm not expecting much, though. It'll be something to watch and get mild entertainment from it.

Wait so hold on, We spend a whole season building up Black Noir. Lots of screen time with the dude by himself literally storytelling his backstory to the viewer. So now the writers are in a damned if you do, damned if you don't situation. If you bring Noir back, you have solidified that your writers have no balls because they're apparently afraid to kill characters now. If you don't bring him back, his story is a waste. The amount of questions left hanging are wild. Just a few of which are: how the hell does Maeve survive that drop without powers, or survive the shot in the first place? How does Soldierboy come to be in that tube? Why is starlight so useless in every fight? How did this shift in Ryan take place so quickly? Did Maeve nuke a city suburb with neurotoxin? If Butcher was supposed to die after he took V again, why does he get a whole year to live after that anyway? Why should we care about Neumann at all? Overall this episode felt clunky, and the fact that the show is getting milked couldn't be clearer. I came out of the episode feeling confused, unsatisfied, and not particularly thirsty.

Yes, it's true The Boys is the most entertaining show in this genre BUT The Boys is not what most people think of it, tbh. The biggest misconception about The Boys people have, is that it's a "realistic" superhero genre TV series. Really, it's a big problem that people are calling it a "realistic" series for showing mostly the evilness and extreme violence or brutality and other forms of R-rated-ness by so-called superheroes BUT I would say that in terms of realism & fantasy, The Boys is as much of fantasy as MCU movies. Yes, thematically, they both are just fantasies.  The 'reality' is neither full of just goodness, nor just evilness. It has both things in a balanced manner. There is true nuance/greyness, not just either white or black. So, when it comes to portray the idea of 'What if Superheroes existed among us'.... MCU mostly shows the white side of this idea while The Boys mostly shows the black side and over-exaggerates it to many degrees just to appeal us.  But DC is in between. DC shows true greyness/nuance, because that is true reality. A lot of DC is the most realistic among these three.... (yeah I know, I know The Boys was originally made by DC itself). Most probably, a comic-book genre story which is the closest in showing the true realism of that idea is DC's Watchmen (take either graphic novel or the film or TV series). And more examples are - Kingdom Come, V for Vendetta, Batman v Superman, Red Son.
